Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarModule: A 160 W solar module. Output falls with condition. Mount it flat, on a wall or on a solar rack.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HomemadeSolarMod: A 96 W solar module. Output falls with condition. Mount it flat, on a wall or on a solar rack.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarCells: Salvaged from solar gadgets. 16 make a Makeshift Solar Module.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarFlat: Holds 1 module flat on a roof or the ground. Best in summer. Snow stays on it until it melts or you clear it, and storms can crack it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarWall: Holds 1 module on an outside wall facing south or east. Best in winter. Never holds snow, and storms can't crack it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarRackWood: Holds 2 modules tilted toward the sun, on 1 bank input. Good all year. Snow slides off within a few hours in sun or mild air. Storms crack it more than any other mount.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarRackMetal: Holds 2 modules tilted toward the sun, on 1 bank input. Good all year. Snow slides off within a few hours in sun or mild air. Storms rarely crack it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryBox: Holds 2 batteries, 1 inverter and 1 Car Battery Charger. 2 inputs; no room for a charge controller. Place indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryRackWood: Holds 6 batteries, 1 inverter, 2 Car Battery Chargers and 2 charge controllers. Up to 16 inputs with controllers. Place indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryRackMetal: Holds 8 batteries, 1 inverter, 2 Car Battery Chargers and 2 charge controllers. Up to 16 inputs with controllers. Place indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryBankWood: Holds 12 batteries, 2 inverters, 2 Car Battery Chargers and 4 charge controllers. Up to 30 inputs with controllers. Place indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryBankMetal: Holds 16 batteries, 2 inverters, 2 Car Battery Chargers and 4 charge controllers. Up to 30 inputs with controllers. Place indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PlugInInverter: Wire into a battery bank to power the area around it, like a generator. Carries up to 400 W: a fridge-freezer, TV, radio and lights. More than that and the power cuts out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PowerInverter: Wire into a battery bank to power the area around it, like a generator. Carries up to 600 W: a fridge, TV, radio and lights plus a washer or stove. More than that and the power cuts out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_InverterCharger: Carries up to 1000 W from a battery bank. Its built-in 1000 W charger fills the batteries whenever grid or generator power reaches the bank, like 10 Car Battery Chargers.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_MakeshiftInverte: Carries up to 400 W from a battery bank, like a Plug-in Inverter, but loses a quarter of what passes through (a Plug-in Inverter: a tenth), idles at 8 W (a Plug-in Inverter: 4 W) and wears out sooner.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HomemadeInverter: Carries up to 600 W from a battery bank, like a Power Inverter, but loses a fifth of what passes through (a Power Inverter: a tenth), idles at 16 W (a Power Inverter: 8 W) and wears out sooner.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_MicrowaveTransfo: Salvaged from a microwave. Used to make a Makeshift Plug-in Inverter or a Makeshift Power Inverter.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ChargeController: Wire into a battery rack or cabinet to add 7 inputs (a bank has 2 without one). Panels, scoop rotors and treadmills use 1 input; bladed wind chargers use 3. Doesn't fit a battery box.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarFailsafe: Place it under a backup generator. Starts the generator when the battery bank runs low and stops it once the bank recharges.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_DeepCycleBattery: Holds about twice a car battery and lasts 2.5 times the charge cycles. Fits a battery bank or a vehicle.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_L16Battery: Holds 3.5 times a car battery and lasts 5 times the charge cycles. 6 V: battery banks only, not vehicles.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_JarBattery: Holds two-thirds of a car battery but lasts three times its charge cycles. Heavy, and battery banks only.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryCase: Rebuild it into a new, empty battery with fresh Battery Plates and acid.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_WornBatteryPlate: Recast at a furnace: 3 worn sets make 2 Battery Plates and 1 Lead Dross. A Lead Pipe can stand in for the third set.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryPlates: Used to rebuild a battery or make a Jar Battery.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryPlateMold: Used at a furnace to cast Battery Plates. Doesn't break.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryElectroly: 1 L of battery acid. Used to rebuild batteries.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarMaintainer: Clip it to a vehicle to keep its battery charged in daylight.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarCellCharger: Place it outdoors with up to 4 Batteries inside (the small kind, not car batteries). Charges them in daylight.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarGardenLight: Place it on the ground outdoors. Charges by day and glows at night. Swap in a coloured light bulb to change its colour.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_UnmountGivesModu: Gives back the modules, each in the condition it went in.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeApartGivesBu: Gives back the light bulb too, if it has one.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RepairCrackedMod: Adds 15 condition to a cracked module, up to 80, less 10 for each earlier seal. The glass stays cracked.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ReglazeModule: New glass for any damaged module: back to new, and its seal count clears. Takes a flat pane and epoxy; car windows won't do.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeOutWindowGla: Dig the putty out of a window picked up with a crowbar and lift out its two panes. Any other picked-up furniture won't do.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ModuleSealedFull: Sealed as far as sealing goes. Reglaze it in place.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PanelSealedFully: Sealed as far as sealing goes. Reglaze it in place.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ModuleTooLightly: Too lightly cracked for a seal to help: seals reach 80. Reglaze it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeApartShatter: Only a factory Solar Module at 0 condition comes apart, for 12 Solar Cells.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ServiceBattery: Adds 10 condition, up to 20 short of the battery's repair limit (85, less 10 for each time it was repaired): 65 on a battery never reconditioned. Doesn't count as a repair, and its charge stays.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ReconditionBatte: Brings the battery to its repair limit (85, less 10 for each time it was repaired) and leaves it empty. Wood ash does what baking soda does.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RecastBatteryPla: 3 worn sets make 2 Battery Plates and 1 Lead Dross. A Lead Pipe can stand in for the third set. Smelt the dross back into plates with charcoal.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ReduceLeadDross: 1 Lead Dross makes 1 set of Battery Plates, so recast lead is never lost.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_CastBatteryPlate: Three lead pipes cast one set of plates, with no battery case needed: enough for a jar battery.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RebuildCarBatter: Gives back the car battery the case came from, as new and empty.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_MakeJarBattery: Any empty glass jars, or glazed clay jars. The battery comes out as new, and empty.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_GardenLightOutdo: Garden lights go on the ground outdoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BankIndoorsOnly: Battery banks go indoors, inside a building.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NotAPart: Only batteries, inverters, car battery chargers and charge controllers can be wired in.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NothingToWire: Carry a battery, an inverter, a car battery charger or a charge controller to wire it in.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoSlot: The bank has no room for another one of these.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TooDark: It's too dark to see what you're doing.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedSnowTool: Needs a broom or a snow shovel.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedsFittingBlad: Needs blades this wind charger takes.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoInputSlot: The bank has no free input for it. Charge controllers add more, in a battery rack or cabinet.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BankNotConnected: The battery bank isn't connected yet. Connect Bank from its own menu first.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoInverter: The bank has no working inverter.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoBatteries: The bank has no working batteries.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BarrelDigester: Makes gas from food scraps and manure once it gets going, into garbage bags or a Tarp Gas Bag. The smallest digester: smells the most and stops in the cold.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_InsulatedDigeste: Three times the size of a barrel digester. Works into the fall and smells less.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BrickDome: Three times the size of an insulated digester. Build it on earth, grass or sand. Keeps itself warm on its own gas, works all winter and hardly smells. Hard to build.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_WoodAsh: Compostable. Works like baking soda for servicing a battery, settles a sour digester, and makes a scrubber's water last longer.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_LeadDross: Smelt with charcoal at a furnace for 1 set of Battery Plates.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoSludge: Not enough sludge to fill a bag.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedsSack: Needs an empty sack or a compost bag with room in it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoGasBags: Only a barrel digester takes gas bags.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoGasBag: There's no gas bag on it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NotBarrel: Only a barrel digester can be upgraded.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TarpGasBag: Gas holder for a barrel digester. Holds 1 m³ (garbage bags: 0.6) and lasts about 4 times as long.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_IronSponge: Packs a digester's scrubber in place of Steel Wool. Air it out with a little water, clean or tainted, to reuse it; each airing costs 1 condition.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SpentIronSponge: Air it out with a little water, clean or tainted, to get an Iron Sponge back, at 1 less condition.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeSludge: Spent sludge comes out as compost. The tank slows once it's nearly full.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_VentGas: Lets the gas out, so a gas bag can come off. Careful indoors: it fills the building with fumes for a while.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FitGarbageBags: Cheap and quick, but they tear before long.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FitTarpGasBag: Holds 1 m³ of gas (garbage bags: 0.6) and lasts about 4 times as long.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeOffGasBag: A tarp gas bag comes off whole, to mend or fit elsewhere. Garbage bags are done for.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_Upgrade: Makes it an Insulated Digester: three times the size, holds more feed and works into the fall. What's inside the barrel stays.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FillByPump: Slow, tiring work that only fills it partway.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FillByCompressor: Runs the digester's compressor to fill it all the way, once the gas is scrubbed.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FitScrubber: Cleans the gas so a compressor can fill a tank all the way. Keep its water and packing refilled.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FitCompressor: Wires a fridge compressor to the gas holder. Where the digester has power, it fills tanks all the way with scrubbed gas.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberWa: 4 L of plain water, clean or tainted, from any container you carry cleans the gas for a while.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberAs: Wood ash in the water makes it last longer.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberLi: Quicklime in the water makes it last longest.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberWo: Steel wool catches what the water misses. Pack in fresh once it's spent.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberSp: Packs it in place of steel wool. The spent sponge comes back out at the next packing, to air out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_GasConversionKit: Fit it to a generator so it runs on gas from a digester or gasifier instead of gasoline. Carries up to 3000 W on biogas; less on wood gas, which also wears the generator faster.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HasKit: This generator already has a Gas Conversion Kit.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoKit: This generator has no Gas Conversion Kit.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HasLine: A gas line is already connected.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_DigesterOutOfRea: The digester is too far away, or on another floor.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoDigesterInReac: No digester within %1 squares on this floor, and no gasifier beside the generator.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RemoveKitFirst: Remove the Gas Conversion Kit first.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedsVessel: Needs a propane tank, a welding torch or a propane lantern bottle.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoPower: The digester has no power to run its compressor.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PumpLimit: A tire pump can't push it any fuller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedsScrubbed: Past what a tire pump can push, the compressor needs scrubbed gas: refill the scrubber.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoGasToFill: There's no gas in the holder.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TooLittleGas: There's too little gas in the holder to fill it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FridgeCompressor: Fit it to a powered digester to fill propane tanks all the way with scrubbed biogas. Also inflates tires wherever there's power.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_GasHeater: Place it beside a digester. Burns a little of its biogas to keep the digester, or a cold room, warm.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoDigesterNear: There's no digester with gas beside it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PrimitiveGasifie: Burns wood to make gas for a generator beside it with a Gas Conversion Kit. Small, tarry and needs cleaning often.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_Gasifier: Burns wood to make gas for a generator beside it with a Gas Conversion Kit. A full hopper runs it nearly as long as a tank of gasoline.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_AdvancedGasifier: Burns wood or, best, charcoal to make gas for a generator beside it with a Gas Conversion Kit. Little tar and little cleaning.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TarryPacking: Burn it in a gasifier's hopper.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoWood: There's no wood in the hopper.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_LittleAsh: There's too little ash to clean out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_GasifierNotBesid: A gasifier must stand right beside the generator.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_WontTakeCondensa: That won't take it. Drained hot, it needs metal, glass or a pot.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HasBulb: The light already has a bulb.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_CantAttachMainta: It needs a battery, and no maintainer already clipped on.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoMaintainerAtta: No solar maintainer is clipped on.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_CantSwitchLamps: The switch is shut in the battery box, or already set so.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TreadmillMotor: Powers a Scoop Rotor or Treadmill Wind Charger.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ScoopRotor: Weak and slow, but it turns in any wind and never needs the brake. Uses 1 bank input, like a panel; no charge controller needed.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TreadmillNotConn: Connect it to a bank first, or the running goes nowhere.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TreadmillNoPower: There's no power for its motor. Connect it to a battery bank, and running on it makes power instead.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RunOnTreadmill: Half an hour of running. Connected to a battery bank, it charges the bank; otherwise the treadmill runs off the power like any appliance.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ConnectTreadmill: Wires the motor to make power instead of using it, and connects the treadmill to this bank, so running on it charges the bank's batteries. It uses one of the bank's inputs.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_UnwireTreadmill: Wires the motor back to run off the power like any appliance, and takes the treadmill out of its bank. The wire comes back.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ConnectSource: Wires it into this bank, so what it makes charges the bank's batteries. A panel, scoop rotor or treadmill uses one of the bank's inputs; the other wind chargers use three.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_DisconnectSource: Unwires it from its bank, which stops taking its power.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_Brake: Stops the blades, so a gale can't break them. A braked charger makes nothing.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ReleaseBrake: Lets the blades turn again, to make power.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ClearSnow: Snow takes the share of the panel it covers off its output. Sweeping it off gets that back.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TreadmillWindCha: Turns a Treadmill Motor in the wind. Set the brake in a gale or the blades may break. Uses 3 inputs, so the bank needs a charge controller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_CarAlternatorWin: Turns a Car Alternator in the wind, for more power than a Treadmill Wind Charger. Set the brake in a gale or the blades may break. Uses 3 inputs, so the bank needs a charge controller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TimberTreadmillW: The Treadmill Wind Charger on three lashed logs instead of a welded mast: the same power, built with Carpentry. Set the brake in a gale or the blades may break. Uses 3 inputs, so the bank needs a charge controller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TimberCarAlterna: The Car Alternator Wind Charger on three lashed logs instead of a welded mast: the same power, built with Carpentry. Set the brake in a gale or the blades may break. Uses 3 inputs, so the bank needs a charge controller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_WindTurbine: The strongest wind charger. In a gale it turns out of the wind but keeps most of its output, and its blades take 20 km/h more wind before they break than on other chargers. Uses 3 inputs, so the bank needs a charge controller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_Blades: All three blades for any bladed wind charger; a spare set replaces a broken one. Holds in a stronger gale than plastic pipe, a weaker one than steel.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PipeBlades: All three blades for any bladed wind charger; a spare set replaces a broken one. Breaks in the weakest gale of any set.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SteelBlades: All three blades for any bladed wind charger; a spare set replaces a broken one. Holds in the strongest gale. A Blast Furnace melts it down.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BrokenSteelBlade: A Blast Furnace melts the steel back out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HomemadeAlternat: Powers a Homemade Wind Turbine, the strongest wind charger.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_CarAlternator: Powers a Car Alternator Wind Charger. Take one out of an intact car's engine, or find one when scrapping a smashed wreck.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NotACar: Only an intact car's engine has an alternator to work on.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_AlternatorGone: This car's alternator has already been taken out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_AlternatorFitted: This car still has its alternator.
